items.q: The graph of variation of GFR with plasma concentration is divided into overt renal failure and the:
opts: Zone of overfiltration and protein overload
Hyperfiltration plateau of the early phase
items.exp: Graph zones: overt renal failure (GFR <25%) and zone of compensation (adequate renal reserve). (Book p807)

items.q: Curve A on that graph — creatinine, urea and uric acid — behaves how?
opts: Depends largely on GFR for excretion; inverse relation with GFR
Rises only in the late stage of CKD, like the B curve
Stays normal throughout CRF, like the sodium curve
Follows the uric acid curve in overt renal failure
items.exp: A: creatinine, urea, uric acid — depend largely on GFR for excretion; inverse relation with GFR. (Book p807)

items.q: The substances named under curve B are:
items.exp: B: PO₄, uric acid, K, H — ↑ only in late stage of CKD. (Book p807)

items.q: Curve B substances rise only in the late stage of CKD.
opts: False — they stay normal in CRF
items.exp: B: PO₄, uric acid, K, H — ↑ only in late stage of CKD. (Book p807)

items.q: The mechanism for curve B is that the tubules increase excretion as GFR declines by:
items.exp: B: tubules increase excretion as GFR declines — either by secretion or decreased reabsorption. (Book p807)
C: sodium — normal throughout CRF (chronic renal failure); rate of excretion of Na per surviving nephron increases. (Book p807)

items.q: Match the following substance to its curve — 1) Creatinine  2) Phosphate  3) Sodium … A) Normal throughout CRF  B) Inverse relation with GFR  C) Rises only in late CKD
items.exp: A: creatinine (inverse with GFR); B: phosphate (late CKD); C: sodium (normal throughout CRF). (Book p807)

items.q: All but one rise only in the late stage of CKD per curve B. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: B (late CKD): PO₄, uric acid, K, H; creatinine belongs to curve A. (Book p807)

items.q: A patient in the overt-renal-failure zone (GFR 10%) still excretes sodium normally. The graph explains this because:
opts: The rate of Na excretion per surviving nephron increases
The proximal tubule reabsorbs less sodium
items.exp: C: rate of excretion of Na per surviving nephron increases → sodium normal throughout CRF. (Book p807)
